name: Fulfill new orders with Shopify and MySQL in real time

nodes.name: On Shopify Event
nodes.notes: Native push trigger — shopify calls this workflow the moment the event happens (no polling). Credential: Shopify access token. Same Shopify Admin API access token as the Shopify node.

nodes.name: Pull Side A (MySQL)
nodes.notes: Selects rows from the MySQL table (returnAll) — the read side of the store. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Pull Side B (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Order Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Diff the Two Systems
nodes.notes: Diffs two streams by key into 4 lanes: only-in-A, same, different, only-in-B — the heart of the sync.

nodes.name: Create Missing in Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Order Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Count In-Sync Rows
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Apply Updates to Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Order Tracker', matched on orderId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Backfill into MySQL
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Gather Sync Results
nodes.notes: Rejoins 4 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Sort Orders Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 50 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Append Audit Row (MySQL)
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

# Fulfill new orders with Google Sheets & MySQL

**Pattern:** Order Fulfillment · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers inventory work end to end across Google Sheets, MySQL, Slack, Outlook and Shopify.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. On Shopify Event
2. Pull Side A (MySQL)
3. Pull Side B (Google Sheets)
4. Diff the Two Systems
5. Create Missing in Google Sheets
6. Count In-Sync Rows
7. Apply Updates to Google Sheets
8. Backfill into MySQL
9. Gather Sync Results
10. Save Execution Metadata
11. Sort Orders Newest First
12. Align Field Names
13. Stamp Processing Time
14. Cap Batch Volume
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (MySQL)
17. Send Summary to Outlook

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing inventory work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

On Shopify Event → Pull Side A (MySQL) → Pull Side B (Google Sheets) → Diff the Two Systems → Create Missing in Google Sheets → Count In-Sync Rows → Apply Updates to Google Sheets → Backfill into MySQL → Gather Sync Results → Save Execution Metadata → Sort Orders Newest First → Align Field Names → Stamp Processing Time → Cap Batch Volume → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (MySQL) → Send Summary to Outlook → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and MySQL aligned by hand for inventory
- Reconciling Google Sheets against MySQL after the two quietly drifted apart
- Pushing inventory events into Google Sheets and MySQL the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Inventory work where "Pull Side A (MySQL)" is still a manual step before Google Sheets

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and MySQL in step for inventory, without anyone re-typing a row
- Compares Google Sheets against MySQL before writing, so only genuine differences land
- A failed Google Sheets or MySQL call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this inventory build
- Every inventory run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for inventory

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; MySQL connection; Shopify access token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Compare Datasets does the matching instead of hand-rolled join logic — one node produces four labeled lanes (only-in-A, matching, different, only-in-B), and each lane gets exactly the action it needs (create / count / update / backfill) instead of one generic 'sync' branch trying to cover every case.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Swap Side A or Side B for a third platform and rewire the merge-by-fields key.
2. Intentionally create a mismatch between the two systems and trace which lane it lands in.
3. Change mergeByFields to a different key and see how the diff results shift.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Shopify access token**
Same Shopify Admin API access token as the Shopify node.
_Gotcha:_ n8n registers the webhook on activation; the token needs the matching read scope or registration silently fails.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your inventory process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- MySQL: grant the user only the tables this workflow touches; avoid `GRANT ALL` on the schema.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.

**Do not log**
inventory payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.
